result_text:
The validator passes with no findings.

## Recommendation
**Don't expand Assist yet, and don't book any responder-hour savings.** The data doesn't show that Assist sped up recovery. Within every severity level, incidents closed slower in the Assist week.

The headline drop in median time to close is a mix effect. The cutover week's incidents were mostly low-severity, and that alone pulls the overall median down.

## What the data shows
| | Manual week | Assist week |
|---|---|---|
| Median time to close | 7.27h | 5.44h |
| Mean time to close | 7.14h | 7.53h |
| Median responder minutes | 87 | 69 |
| Mean responder minutes | 90 | 91 |
| sev3 share of incidents | 47% | 73% |
| sev1 share of incidents | 13% | 7% |

- **Slower within every severity.** Median time to close was higher in the Assist week at each level, and the 95% bootstrap intervals exclude zero. The wording below is associative only, because nothing here identifies a cause.

  | Severity | Median time to close, manual | Median time to close, Assist | Median responder minutes, manual | Median responder minutes, Assist |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | sev1 | 18.3h | 27.7h | 242 | 311 |
  | sev2 | 8.5h | 12.3h | 99.5 | 139.5 |
  | sev3 | 2.8h | 5.0h | 39 | 65 |

- **Standardized to the manual week's severity mix**, the Assist week is about 3.8h and about 37 responder minutes slower per incident.
- **The responders' complaint matches the data.** The hardest incidents look worse under Assist. Of 9 sev1 incidents with recorded closures in the Assist week, 1 reopened within 72 hours, against none of 28 in the manual week.
- **Responder-hours.** The credible attributable savings are zero. Total recorded responder minutes were roughly flat (18,857 manual vs 18,175 Assist), and the small drop is explained by fewer incidents with recorded closure and the severity mix.

## Why the data can't settle causation
There was no holdout, so nothing here identifies Assist's effect in either direction.
- **Staffing rose at the cutover.** Responders went from 12 to 14 in identity and 11 to 13 in storage. A real Assist benefit could be masked by other changes.
- **Interruptions changed in the Assist week.** Interruption minutes were also higher on several Assist days.
- **The severity mix may be downstream of Assist.** If Assist changed how incidents get triaged or classified, standardizing on severity is itself biased.
- **Closure records are incomplete.** 11 of 420 incidents have no closure record: 1 in the manual week, 10 in the Assist week, including 5 of 14 sev1. I can't tell whether those are unclosed, unrecorded or unexported, so the direction of any bias is unknown. Only 9 Assist-week sev1 incidents have a recorded closure, so the sev1 numbers are thin.
- **Handoffs.** Sev1 handoffs dropped to a median of 0 in the Assist week. I didn't investigate whether that is real or a recording change.

## Suggested next step
Run a staggered or holdout rollout in one or two more service groups. First reconcile the 10 missing Assist-week closures and the sev1 reopen and handoff records. `causal-identification-review` would be the right tool for designing that comparison, and `decision-analysis` for what to do while it runs; I didn't check whether either is installed.

The ledger is in `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s15-pre-3-szny70uq/work/ledger.md`, and the analysis script is `a.py` in the same folder.
